Our wrapper (src/client/javascripts/components/accessible-autocomplete.js, the same file in both) is adapted from HMRC Frontend's accessible-autocomplete component at commit 8aba9fc0b60a193d69fea0d3435a5b504cb922c4. HMRC's wrapper takes its options from data attributes and offers no templates hook, so the hooks go on the alphagov library through our wrapper.

How: pass the library's documented templates.suggestion option from the wrapper. It receives only the suggestion, so the wrapper's source function keeps the last query for it. The template HTML-escapes the suggestion text first, then wraps each case-insensitive match of the query in <strong class="app-autocomplete__match">. Built as a small progressive-enhancement module registered in the existing client bundle (no new webpack entry). It listens for the change event inc-202 adds, and reads a country-to-prefix map the server builds with the same prefix rule as validation, so subdivisions map to their parent.

Hide approach (Sam, 20 Oct): the server always renders the prefix element, through the GOV.UK input's prefix with classes "app-js-only" and an inner span holding the saved country's code (empty before a pick, so the slot exists). CSS hides .app-js-only and shows it only under body.govuk-frontend-supported, the class GOV.UK's page template sets when its JavaScript can run. The script updates the span. Chosen over a script-added prefix because the shown-again and error cases then show the right code at once, with nothing to compute or flash in, and without JavaScript nothing shows.

Validation check, 20 Oct: the stored code does not depend on the prefix being shown. The server joins the saved country's code to what was typed (validate.js regionCodeFrom, from prefixFor(country)) and strips a prefix the trader typed themselves (suffixOf), and the 5-character limit is measured after that. So hiding the prefix without JavaScript changes nothing the server does.
